assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and the later giant TMR in MgO barriers turned spin-dependent tunnelling into the read-head and MRAM technology that underlies modern data storage. It is a clear, reproducible effect with a well-understood electronic-structure origin (symmetry-selective Delta-1 tunnelling), which makes it a very clean case of fundamental magnetism leading to application.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported large room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin's group realized the coherent MgO-based junctions and their industrial development. The supplied trio covers the discovery and the optimization well. The coherent-tunnelling MgO result is also associated with Yuasa and Djayaprawira, who are not in the credited names, so the 2004 step is not fully covered by this configuration.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of confirmation, universal industrial adoption and a theoretical understanding verified by first-principles calculations. The field has had ample time to settle, and recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for the MgO coherent-tunnelling step is split with people outside the credited list.
The 2007 prize for giant magnetoresistance may be seen as partly overlapping, although TMR is a distinct physical mechanism.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new platform in which flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity are tunable in a single device. The prediction of magic angles from a continuum band-structure model, followed by experiment, is an unusually tight link between theory and measurement and has spawned the whole moire quantum-materials field.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 flat-band prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 experiments. The experimental first author Yuan Cao is not among the credited names, and Jarillo-Herrero's role is shared with his co-workers. The supplied names still give a plausible theory-plus-experiment configuration.
assessment.maturity: Highly reproducible across many groups, but the origin of the superconductivity and the nature of the correlated states are still debated, so the interpretation is not fully settled. Recognition is somewhat early, though the discovery is unambiguous.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and the full phase diagram remain debated.
Credit between theory prediction and experiment, and the omission of the leading experimental student, complicate attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator introduced a new classification of electronic phases grounded in spin-orbit coupling and band topology. The idea has been confirmed with band-structure calculations and ARPES in real materials, which is where first-principles electronic-structure theory demonstrated its predictive power.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 quantum spin Hall insulator, and Molenkamp's group observed the effect in HgTe quantum wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and the 3D-topological-insulator authors, are outside the credited names, so some decisive contributions are not covered.
assessment.maturity: Nearly two decades of independent confirmation across 2D and 3D systems. Mature and stable, although the 2016 prize recognized topological phase transitions, so overlap needs careful framing.
uncertainties: The credited names omit Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the 3D topological insulator discoverers.
Possible perceived overlap with the 2016 topological-matter prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave the first controllable, non-perturbative treatment of the Mott transition and strongly correlated materials, and in combination with density-functional methods it is the standard tool for realistic correlated-electron calculations. Its conceptual clarity (the infinite-dimension limit and the local self-energy) and its large practical reach are both substantial.
assessment.attribution: Georges and Kotliar developed the mapping onto a self-consistent impurity problem; Vollhardt contributed through the infinite-dimension limit work with Metzner. Metzner and Vollhardt's 1989 limit paper is the origin, and Metzner is not in the credited list, so the founding step is shared outside this configuration.
assessment.maturity: Developed over three decades, widely applied and benchmarked against experiments and cluster extensions. Theory prizes in this area are rare, and predictions for specific materials remain uneven, which reduces the force of the case relative to experimental discoveries.
uncertainties: Metzner's role in the founding limit is not covered by the credited names.
Predictive accuracy for real materials varies, and the committee may favour discoveries over methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength trapping idea, reduced fractional uncertainty to the 10^-18 level and has enabled tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. The idea is simple, original and has delivered record precision.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept; Ye's group drove it to the highest accuracy and stability, with strong contributions also from several other clock groups. Two names fit the pairing well, but credit is shared with others in the clock community, including Hall and Hansch's earlier comb work already recognized in 2005.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with many independent clocks agreeing at the 10^-18 level. The redefinition of the second is pending, which suggests timing is about right.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with prior frequency-comb recognition.
Other groups contributed decisively to clock performance and are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 observation of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model and was the result of two of the largest scientific instruments built. The experimental discovery is of the highest scientific importance, with direct relevance to the mechanism of mass generation.
assessment.attribution: The prize rules limit laureates to three persons, and the collaborations contain thousands. The supplied names are the founders and spokespeople-level leaders of the proposals, a defensible but contested representation of collective work. The theorists were honoured in 2013.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with measurements of couplings and spin-parity confirmed by both experiments. Recognition of the experimental side has been long awaited.
uncertainties: Attributing a collaboration discovery to three individuals is inherently contested.
Other leaders, such as spokespersons at the time of discovery, may be favoured over the founding proposers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices realizes Hubbard-type model Hamiltonians with tunable parameters and single-site resolution, and it gives access to many-body physics (Mott insulators, magnetism, dynamics) that is hard to reach with classical simulation. From a materials-theory view this is an important testbed for the models we use, though quantitative reach for real materials is still limited.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Jaksch supplied key theoretical proposals; Greiner, Bloch and Esslinger drove the experimental realization of the Mott transition and fermionic Hubbard physics. With four credited names and three places, a choice must be made; Zoller is also associated with other candidates in the list. The selected trio is one defensible choice, not the only one.
assessment.maturity: Now a mature, widely reproduced field, though the headline goal of solving open problems such as the Hubbard model phase diagram remains incomplete.
uncertainties: Esslinger's equally strong claim is left out in a three-person selection.
Overlap with earlier recognition of cold-atom cooling and Bose-Einstein condensation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum anomalous Hall effect, predicted from a first-principles model of magnetically doped topological insulators and observed experimentally, gives dissipationless chiral edge transport without an external magnetic field. It is a clean example of electronic-structure theory guiding a magnetism-plus-topology experiment, with metrological promise.
assessment.attribution: Fang and Dai led the 2010 theoretical prediction in Cr/Fe-doped Bi2Se3-family materials, and Xue's group made the 2013 experimental observation. The supplied three names suit this split. Other theory and early-observation contributors, including Haldane's original model, are outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Observed and reproduced by several groups, but the quantization temperature remains low and the field is still developing, so recognition may be somewhat early. A close relationship to the topological-insulator candidate would favour recognizing only one of the two.
uncertainties: Experimental quantization is only reached at very low temperatures.
Overlap with the topological insulator candidate and the Haldane precedent complicate framing.
